question: The O-ring's compression reaction over the squeeze window — the datum 52 replaced with a generous bound, 73 judged the collar wall against, and 87's (A) needs from below.

source.table: Table 2-3: O-Ring Compression Force, p. 2-10 — under 25.4 mm: middle third (hardness below normal) or upper third (above normal) of the bar
source.read: 2026-10-13, vector coordinates of the PDF page (pdftocairo -svg)
source.temperature: §3.8: force decreases very little with temperature except the hardest compounds (N0674-70: −10 % from 24 to 126 °C)
source.time: Parker gives compression set (deflection not recovered after release), not stress relaxation — no field-life force

assumptions: log-load linear in squeeze between the chart's rows
Table 2-3's thirds taken in the log scale the bar is drawn on
seal length = mean circumference on the groove's inner wall (ring stretched onto it)
the unconfined bars hold at an 80 % gland fill

rim_premise_A.is: a clamp at the form 52 prints for the ring's own reaction, (R0 + p) / f(20 y), never lets the rim lift while the lift stays at L0, so the needed reaction is an initial one; a weaker clamp can let the rim lift (it does if the ring keeps its reaction better than the PEEK keeps the clamp, by more than the clamp's margin over L0), a lift is taken as not undone (conservative: under a lift the ledge PEEK creeps at constant load, 52), and the normal force is then what the ring has left; the friction bound runs through the lug ledge (the rim's share can be zero), with µ from 55's dry PEEK–Ti sweep — the ring is greased; temperature is not modelled

missing_data: the compound's own compression-load curve at 15–35 % for CS 1.78 (the band spans compounds)
its stress relaxation over the service life at the capsule's envelope (ISO 3384-type data) — it moves 52's requirement between its two ends
the clamp the bayonet delivers (lug ramp, interference)

temperature: the PEEK in the clamp loop sits between two Ti faces over the same span, so cold unloads the clamp and heat raises it (the loop's compliance sets how fast); the ring's own contraction takes squeeze in the cold, and its force below room temperature is not in the source — every margin here is at the assembly temperature
resin swell (02_02 §3.2 accepts up to 15 % by volume) — it raises the reaction
verdict: The «generous» 100 N is not an upper bound: for a ring under 1" Parker's Table 2-3 puts the 70 Shore A load in the middle or upper third of the Figure 2-4 bar, so the reaction is 96–218 N at the 24.5 % nominal and 160–409 N at the 30 % window top, and the band's top passes 100 N from 17.1 % squeeze. With that top, 52's requirement lies between the clamp at assembly and the 20-year form 52 prints: the lug root at the print floor (SF 2 inside) carries it at the nominal at both ends (1.35× at the worse), at the chain 52 models today (27.3 %) only if the ring has lost about 2 % of its reaction by year 20 (0.98× if it never does), and at the window top only if it has lost about 23 % by year 2 and about 28 % already by year 5 — the PEEK clamp floors within a few years, so the ring's loss is due early (0.72× if it never does, 1.11× at assembly); a ring that does not relax makes the lug bind from 27.1 % (26.8–27.5 % over the transcription's ±4 %), and strength, not printability, then sizes the collar wall — up to 0.28 mm at the window top against the 0.2 mm print floor. From below, the ring starts at no less than 58 N at the 19 % floor — 5.5× what 87's (A) needs with a clamp at the form 52 prints, (R0 + p) / 0.65, which never lets the rim lift while the lift stays at its initial value; a weaker clamp can let the rim lift (whether it does depends on the ring's relaxation, not modelled), a lift is taken as not undone (conservative), and (A) then rests on the ring keeping 18 % of that floor for 20 years. Every margin here holds at the assembly temperature.
